thread:
maya: quick heads up — noticed intermittent NXDOMAINs from edge GPU pods when resolving modelfetch.internal :confused:
jonathan: same, hit it in staging ~20m ago. getaddrinfo hangs for ~3s then returns NXDOMAIN for some nodes only.
sam: any recent changes to nodelocal-dns / resolvConf ordering?
lee: pushed a small change to the node-proxy egress routing yesterday but not touching DNS configs. :eyes:
maya: digging — on an affected node:```
/etc/resolv.conf:
nameserver 127.0.0.53
nameserver 10.100.0.10   # node-local-dns
search staging.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
options ndots:5
```
jonathan: ndots:5 is expected for pods, but that search order can cause append. Try `dig +short modelfetch.internal` vs `dig +short modelfetch.internal.`?
sam: ran both on an affected node:```
$ dig +short modelfetch.internal

# blank (no answer)
$ dig +short modelfetch.internal.
203.0.113.12
```
sam: so unqualified name fails, fully-qualified succeeds. That smells like split-horizon/searchpath append going to the wrong resolver.
maya: interesting — the node-local-dns forwarder is supposed to rewrite internal names to the on-prem forwarder. Looks like some queries with searchpath get forwarded to the public egress NAT and get NXDOMAIN from external DNS.
lee: infra-bot shows recent config change on node-local-dns:```yaml
forwarders:
  - 10.200.1.5   # onprem-dns
  - 8.8.8.8
policy:
  preserve_search: true
```
jonathan: preserve_search:true could be the culprit — when the search is preserved the resolver sends multiple queries with appended domains, public resolver sees unknown and returns NXDOMAIN before the onprem forwarder gets tried?
maya: also seeing UDP truncation on some paths (edge NAT doing UDP->TCP fallback poorly). logs:```
Mar 10 14:02:31 node kernel: conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Mar 10 14:02:32 node systemd-resolved[123]: DNSSEC validation failed for query modelfetch.internal (truncated)
```
sam: conntrack pressure is also real — we had a surge in ephemeral ports from GPU prefetch jobs earlier. conntrack drop + preserve_search could lead to inconsistent answers across pods.
lee: rolling a quick mitigations list:
- disable preserve_search in node-local-dns (rollback)
- temporarily set options ndots:2 in pod resolvconf via init container for affected deployments
- increase conntrack on edge NATs and throttle prefetch jobs
- add a fallback rule to route internal suffix directly to onprem IP (bypass public egress)
maya: can someone take the rollback? I can patch a kube-config and rollout a canary to staging.
jonathan: I'll bump conntrack on the nat-gateway and monitor.
sam: I'll prep an init-container patch to force ndots:2 for the modelfetch pods and do a canary in prod after staging looks good.
infra-bot: deploy-started: node-local-dns rollback to v2.3.1 (canary: k8s/staging nodes 3/10)
maya: canaries show resolution fixed on those nodes (staging) :thumbsup:
lee: conntrack increase applied on nat-gw-3. watching metrics (TCP retries down, UDP drops down)
jonathan: still seeing a few stragglers in ap-southeast — likely older nodes with cached negative entries. negative-ttl was 300s, cache might be serving NXDOMAIN. we should invalidate caches.
sam: doing a rolling restart of node-local-dns daemonset to flush caches in staging.
maya: prod rollback scheduled in 10m after staging green. keep an eye on modelfetch 5xx rates and latency.
lee: note for follow-up: add e2e probes that query both unqualified and fqdn names and assert consistent answers across regions. open a follow-up ticket to audit any service that preserves search before forwarding.
jonathan: thanks all — good catch. filing an incident note with root-cause: combination of preserve_search on forwarder + conntrack exhaustion + negative cache causing split-horizon shadowing.
maya: filing done. closing thread when prod rollback completes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
